title: Letters from Jamaica
subtitle: ‘The Land of Streams and Woods’
omitted_from_reading: The half-title with the printer’s and publishers’ names on its back, the printed contents, and the publishers’ list of works at the end are in the JSON only.
summary: Sketches of Jamaica by a Scottish visitor, published anonymously in 1873; library catalogues give the author as Charles Rampini. He arrived at Kingston one February, probably in 1872, and stayed until the spring with his wife, to whom the book is dedicated. He describes Kingston and Spanish Town, travel by road and the country inns, the Bullhead mountain in the middle of the island, the Manchester mountains around Mandeville, the St. Elizabeth plains, and Bluefields Bay, where he rented a cottage. Other chapters deal with country life, a magistrate’s court, village schools, love-letters, Annancy stories in Jamaican dialect, and obeah. An appendix gives about two hundred Jamaican proverbs. The author’s comments on Black Jamaicans reflect the racial attitudes of his time, and the book uses words now considered offensive.
